summary: Postinstall exfiltrates host recon and cloud/Kubernetes credentials to an anonymous webhook
details: colorpicker-ui@1.2.6 advertises itself as a React color picker but ships a postinstall hook (package.json: "postinstall": "node setup.js") that on npm install runs setup.js and performs bulk installer-side reconnaissance and credential theft. setup.js harvests hostname, whoami, /etc/machine-id, kernel/cgroup/sandbox indicators, mounts, network interfaces/routes/listeners, DNS, process listings, and environment variables. It then queries cloud instance-metadata services to steal IAM credentials: AWS IMDSv1 and IMDSv2 at 169.254.169.254 including /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/<role>, GCP metadata.google.internal service-accounts/default/token, and Azure management.azure.com oauth2/token, and reads the Kubernetes service-account token from /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token. It additionally TCP-scans 127.0.0.1, the default gateway, and the first 20 hosts of the local /24 on ports 22/80/8080 plus a common-ports list. The collected JSON is POSTed in chunks via https.request to a hardcoded webhook at https://webhook.site/3dc365ff-07dd-42e6-b5e7-e70773640ba1fb. Behavior is unrelated to the package's stated purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
